subject: DepotWorks on-prem cluster: safety review and storage/ node-slice recommendations
messages:
From: Alex Romero <alex@depotworks.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: DepotWorks on-prem cluster prep — inventory & safety checks

Hi Vanessa,

Thanks again for taking this on. We're beginning the prep for our first private deployment of Redwood in our Portland colocation. High level: 3 racks, 48U each; mixed nodes (some with 4xA100s, most with dual-socket high-memory) and a small set of NVMe-only caching blades. Primary objective is low-latency inference for our customer-facing inference tier and safe model artifact handling with legal retention controls.

Can you confirm the concrete items your preflight team needs from us and any hard limits (disk encryption, egress firewall rules, snapshot cadence) that will block deployment? I attached an inventory sheet with current node specs.

We also have a corporate KMS (HashiCorp Vault) with an HSM-backed cluster; curious if Redwood needs any special connectors or key wrapping approaches.

Thanks — happy to hop on a quick call.

Alex
Lead Platform Engineer, DepotWorks
(Attachment: depotworks_inventory.xlsx)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Romero <alex@depotworks.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 11:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DepotWorks on-prem cluster prep — inventory & safety checks

Alex — thanks for the inventory and context. High level: we can support your hardware profile but there are a few gating items we'll need clarified before scheduling an on-site rollout. Attaching our preflight checklist for completion (preflight_checklist_v1.pdf).

Immediate asks/notes:
- Node roles: please tag which nodes will be dedicated to inference-GPU, inference-CPU (batch), and model artifact storage. For low-latency routing we recommend at least two active inference-GPU nodes per AZ-equivalent rack.
- Local NVMe: good for KV cache/local scratch. We recommend reserving at least 60% of NVMe for ephemeral cache (tmp model segments) and 40% for OS/containers to avoid eviction storms.
- Persistent model store: we prefer a resilient blockstore behind a PV class with volume snapshot support (hourly snapshot for first 48 hours during rollout).
- Encryption: KMS integration is supported via wrapped keys. Our usual pattern is customer KMS -> SKI-wrapped model keys stored in Redwood control plane (customer-managed key policy). We'll follow up with a short KMS integration spec.
- Network: outbound egress must permit reachability to our control-plane endpoints on ports 443/8443 and allow selective metrics export ports for Prometheus. Also need L2/L3 isolation between inference plane and admin plane.

Can Karthik and Monica weigh in on recommended node-sizing and PV profiles; I'll schedule a 30-min deep-dive with your infra lead after we validate the checklist.

Best,
Vanessa Ortiz
Strategic Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: preflight_checklist_v1.pdf)

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Tue, 20 Mar 2028 14:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DepotWorks on-prem cluster prep — node sizing and storage guidance

Vanessa / Monica — notes for the checklist and for Alex when we speak: consolidate these into the preflight doc and I'll upload to the drive.

Node grid proposal (high level):
- control-plane: 3 x 16 vCPU / 64GB, non-gpu, high-availability, taint: node-role.kubernetes.io/control=NoSchedule
- infra (monitoring, ingress, registry): 3 x 8 vCPU / 32GB, medium IO, PV class: fast-block-ssd (replicated)
- inference-gpu (latency tier): 4–6 x nodes with 2xA100 or equivalent, 1TB host RAM, local NVMe (2TB) for shard cache. Taints: inference=latency:NoSchedule, tolerations applied by Redwood daemonset.
- inference-cpu (batch/async): 6–8 x dual-socket high-memory nodes, large ephemeral storage for batched workloads.
- model-store (artifact backing): 3–5 x blockstore nodes with encrypted backends (Ceph/Rook or SAN), PV class: model-ssd-replicated, snapshot-enabled.

Storage policy details:
- PV classes: model-ssd-replicated (encryption-at-rest, replication factor >=3), fast-block-ssd (for infra and registry), local-nvme-ephemeral (for KV cache).
- Snapshot cadence: during rollout hourly snapshots for first 48 hours then daily for 7 days, then retain weekly for 30 days.
- Eviction / QoS: set eviction thresholds aggressively for low-latency pool: node.kubernetes.io/eviction-hard: memory.available<200Mi,nodefs.available<10% and reduce pod disruption budgets for model-cache.
- Disk encryption: customer KMS integration recommended. If KMS is unavailable, use host LUKS with passphrase managed via sealed-secrets.
- Backup/restore: off-cluster backups for model artifacts to S3-compatible target behind private VPC endpoint. Verify bandwidth constraints during initial sync — prefer throttled seeding.

Networking notes:
- Ingress: edge LB in front of the latency pool; advertise VIPs inside the customer VPC.
- Egress firewall: allow our control-plane CIDR and Prometheus scrape endpoints.
- NTP and DNS stability important for certificate validation during rollout.

I'll draft a concrete resource manifest (node selectors, storageclass snippets, tolerations) and link it into the Drive.

Karthik
Director, Infrastructure Products, Redwood Inference

From: Alex Romero <alex@depotworks.com>
To: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 08:02:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DepotWorks on-prem cluster prep — inventory & safety checks

Thanks Karthik — that's helpful. Couple follow-ups from our infra/security team after reviewing the checklist and your sizing: 

1) Backup window: what's the typical bandwidth/time to seed a 4TB model store to the S3 target? We have a 500Mbps pipeline to our DR site.
2) KMS: we use HashiCorp Vault with HSM — we'll need specifics on key-wrapping interfaces and any agent that Redwood would run. Is there an approved HSM vendor list?
3) Can you confirm the recommended PV reclaimPolicy for model artifacts (Retain vs Delete) given compliance requirements?

Attached is our encryption requirements doc — please call out any gaps.

Alex
(Attachment: encryption_requirements.docx)

From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa_ortiz@redwood.ai>
To: Alex Romero <alex@depotworks.com>
Cc: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>, Monica Patel <monica_patel@redwood.ai>
Date: Wed, 21 Mar 2028 10:20:00 -0700
Subject: Re: DepotWorks on-prem cluster prep — inventory & safety checks

Alex — quick summary and next steps so nothing falls through the cracks: 

Action items assigned:
- DepotWorks: complete the attached preflight checklist and mark node roles in the inventory sheet (due: 2028-03-24) — Alex.
- Redwood (Karthik): produce resource manifest snippets (nodeSelector/taints/tolerations/StorageClass examples) and a snapshot policy template (ETA: 2028-03-22).
- Redwood (Monica): draft KMS integration notes including Vault agent pattern and HSM vendor compatibility matrix (ETA: 2028-03-23).
- Joint: 30-min call to validate bandwidth/snapshot plan and confirm PV reclaim policy (scheduled tentatively for 2028-03-25 10:00 PT).

Answers to the immediate questions you raised:
- Seeding 4TB over a 500Mbps link: theoretical minimum ~18 hours; with overheads and throttling plan assume 24–36 hours. We'll propose a phased seeding (hot models first) to reduce downtime.
- PV reclaimPolicy: for model artifacts we recommend Reclaim=Retain (compliance-friendly) and implement an automated lifecycle job to prune and archive artifacts to off-cluster object storage after retention windows expire.
- KMS/HSM: Vault HSM-backed clusters are supported. We'll provide the exact KMS API call patterns and an optional lightweight Vault sidecar for key unwrap during node bootstrap.

I've uploaded Karthik and Monica's drafts and our summary to the shared Drive (see link in metadata). Please confirm the call time and we'll lock calendar.

Best,
Vanessa
Strategic Sales Engineer, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: deployment_plan_v0.1.xlsx)
